framing_judgment_87000x.reasoning: Work-normalized TFLOPS is the fair metric and is what the coder used; raw us would favor AXIOM (1/4096 the work). The caveat is stated explicitly and repeatedly (dims.note, fairness_caveat, BENCHMARKS.md, DESIGN 3.1.19): AXIOM computes 1 output row via 1 workgroup (~1 of ~188 SMs, dispatch-latency-dominated), llama.cpp computes 4096 rows tiled across all SMs. The DESIGN explicitly decomposes the gap into (1) 1/4096 work and (2) dispatch-latency domination. No conflation is hidden.
framing_judgment_87000x.recommendation: RECOMMEND (non-blocking) adding a multi-row context number. examples/q4km_dequant_matmul.axc (M3.1, computes ALL rows) exists but is a naive scalar matmul at K=256 (NOT K=14336, NOT coopmat), so it would isolate the per-row-efficiency gap from the work-size gap. This is a useful additional data point but NOT required for the kill-criterion: DESIGN 5 names the Q4_K_M kernel and the FROZEN M2.6 matvec IS the kernel under test. The single-row-matvec-vs-GEMV comparison fairly represents 'AXIOM's current Q4_K_M kernel vs llama.cpp' and does NOT overstate the gap given the prominent caveat.
